ABOUT THE AUTHOR: Born in Bowraville NSW, Allen Gillon qualified as a Teacher for the NSW Department Of Education in 1964, spending almost 25 years as a Primary Teacher. During that time Mr Gillon completed additional courses in musical arrangement at Sydney Conservatorium Of Music. He has written and had published a number of classroom texts, currently in use in Australian Schools. His musical training and experience resulted in his being granted many play and drama assignments, including a huge production of
“Oliver” in the Penrith Department Region in 1977, co-ordinating 3 Primary schools, a 250 piece choir and a 13 member orchestra. Mr Gillon’s love of writing and school performances led him to write and produce many plays. Public acceptance and the success of these plays led to the production of this publication.

HOPE THEY LEARNED A LESSON! Audiences love this humorous yet emotional play highlighting the diffic ulties associated with intolerance, disabilities, one-punch cowardly hits and bullying.
THE STORY Dominic Lollo is a new boy at the school. He lost an arm ina car accident. Most of the pupils accept him except “Spider” Townley and his “gang” - boys and girls. Relationships simmer until Spider accidently falls overboard from a stolen fishing boat. Dominic, diving in from the shoreline, rescues Spider - the others can’t swim. The resulting Courtroom drama leaves the audience applauding.
Act 4 can involve parents as “Judges” (instead of the Applause Machine). Act 6 requires a small “tinny” in front of stage with fishing gear and anchor etc. A local Parent may get involved in setting up an imaginary river and boat scene. Spider falls in and Dominic rescues him - front of stage. Act 7, the Courtroom scene, could include a couple of “popular” teachers out of character, dancing the “Lollipop” song.
SONGS “My Boy Lollipop” “Show A Little Kindness” “You'll Never Walk Alone” “The Other Man’s Grass” TALENT QUEST “Redback On The Toilet Seat” “Yellow Submarine” Many other songs and dances according to time-limits.
LENGTH The Other Man’s Grass is about 1 hour long. It may be lengthened or shortened in ACT 4, the Talent Quest. An interval could be included before ACT 4.
